messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@finovatebank.com>, Claire Johnson <claire.johnson@finovatebank.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Feb 2026 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Stakeholder mapping & next steps — Finovate Bank

Thanks again for taking the time earlier, Samir & Claire — great discussion. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned.

Highlights from the call
- Key outcomes: confirm technical fit for LLM-powered customer triage; expected 50k messages/month initial volume with 95th pct latency target ~300ms token latency.
- Primary decision criteria: latency & cost per token, SOC2/compliance posture, vendor-managed MLPs vs private deployment options, and procurement timeline (Q2 budget).

Stakeholder mapping (as discussed) — can you confirm these roles/contacts?
- Champion (technical): Samir Patel, Director of ML (you) — confirmed.
- Economic buyer: Michael O'Neil, CFO (Samir, please confirm).
- Legal: Kate Morales (I believe Kate is the right contact; please confirm).
- Security/compliance: Liam Brown / security team (we discussed encryption-at-rest and key management).
- Procurement: procurement@finovatebank.com (to handle SOW/MSA and pricing).

Attachments I’m sharing: ROI-deck-Finovate-Redwood.pdf (high-level ROI + TCO model), SOC2-Summary.pdf (controls overview).

Proposed next steps
1) Samir to confirm stakeholder list and target decision date (you mentioned end of Q2).
2) Redwood to share pricing sheet and mutual action plan (I’ve attached a draft).
3) Schedule two follow-ups: procurement call (procurement + finance) and a short legal checklist call (Kate or legal lead) to surface any redlines.
4) I’ll send a short talk-track pack for Samir to use with the CFO (economic buyer) focusing on ROI and cost predictability.

Open questions for you
- Is the CFO available for a 20–30 minute budget conversation the week of Mar 8?
- Any additional compliance evidence we should prioritize (e.g., encryption key management, tenant isolation)?

Thanks — I’ll wait for confirmation and will schedule the procurement/legal calls once you confirm contacts.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference
---
Attachments: ROI-deck-Finovate-Redwood.pdf (pdf), SOC2-Summary.pdf (pdf)

- Confirmed: I’ll own the technical evaluation + championing internally.
- Economic buyer: Michael O'Neil (CFO) — I can intro you via email; he’s focused on predictable unit economics and integration overhead.
- Legal: looping in Kate Morales (cc’d) — she’ll advise on MSA and DPIA requirements.

Couple of asks from my side:
1) Can you share the detailed pricing sheet and the mutual action plan (MAP) so we can align internally?
2) A short one-pager I can forward to Michael that summarizes ROI and the ask (30–60s read) would be helpful.
3) We have a data residency question: some data will remain in our VPC, but we need to understand what goes to Redwood-hosted instances vs private — can you outline deployment options in the MAP?

If those materials are ready I’ll schedule a brief internal sync and then connect Michael for the budget convo (likely week of Mar 8).

Samir

Appreciate the quick turnaround, Samir — and thanks Kate for joining.

Attached: pricing-sheet.xlsx, mutual-action-plan.docx. I also added a one-page ROI summary that you can forward to Michael (also included in the ROI deck).

Quick answers inline:
- Deployment options: see MAP section 2 — Hosted API (fastest to prod), Dedicated (reserved GPU capacity in our cloud region for data isolation), Private (VPC/on-prem for fully customer-managed network). I highlighted recommended options for your use case (start hosted -> dedicated if throughput grows -> private if policy requires).
- Data residency: For Hosted we can pin region and provide KMS integrations; for Private, all model inference stays in your VPC. I’ve flagged the MAP for where we need legal + security to confirm SLA and data-flow diagrams.

Champion enablement (Samir) — short talk track for Michael (economic buyer):
- Headline: Reduce triage operating costs by ~35% while improving first-contact resolution and maintaining regulatory controls.
- Cost angle: predictable committed pricing with clear per-token & per-embedding unit economics; conservative TCO in the ROI deck accounts for batching & caching improvements.
- Risk/controls: SOC2 controls + KMS/HSM options; optional Private deployment for strict data isolation.
- Ask: 20–30 min budget alignment to confirm committed capacity and procurement cadence.

Next steps (proposed)
1) Procurement call: procurement@finovatebank.com + Rafael to walk pricing and PO/contracting process — propose Wed, Mar 10, 11am PT.
2) Legal/data call: Kate + Vivek to review MSA/DPA + SOC2 artifacts — propose Thu, Mar 11, 9am PT.
3) Budget intro: Michael + Samir + Marissa — propose Mar 9 or Mar 10 30 min slot.

Rafael will own the procurement walkthrough; I’ll prepare the short slide for Michael and the MAP updates.

Regards,
Marissa
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
